2607.29254.title: Tool Specifications Matter: Uncovering and Mitigating Safety Risks in AI Agents
2607.29254.paper_summary: AI agents extend large language models (LLMs) with external tools, enabling them to perform complex tasks and translate model outputs into consequential real-world actions. Yet LLMs often become substantially less safe when deployed as agents, and the source of this degradation remains poorly understood. In this paper, we identify schema-formatted tool specifications as a primary source of agent safety degradation and show, through white-box representation analysis, that they weaken the model's internal refusal signals and contribute to unsafe tool execution. Building on this finding, we propose SafeKeep, an inference-time safeguard that decouples safety judgment from tool execution: it assesses requests using flattened textual tool specifications while retaining the original schema-formatted specifications for execution. Across two representative benchmarks and four LLMs, including both white-box and black-box models, SafeKeep increases the average refusal rate for harmful requests from 23.8% to 70.6% and reduces the average attack success rate under observation-level prompt injection from 25.6% to 2.5%. It also outperforms existing safeguards and preserves task-handling capability. We release the code and data at https://github.com/snowcatsmoking/SafeKeep .
2607.29254.paper_summary_zh: AI 代理擴展了大型語言模型 (LLMs) 與外部工具，使它們能夠執行複雜任務並將模型輸出轉化為重要的現實行動。<lb/>然而，當 LLMs 作為代理部署時，通常會顯著降低安全性，而這種降級的來源仍然不甚了解。<lb/>在本文中，我們確定了以架構格式化的工具規範作為代理安全性降級的主要來源，並通過白盒表示分析顯示，它們削弱了模型的內部拒絕信號並促成了不安全的工具執行。<lb/>基於這一發現，我們提出了 SafeKeep，一種推理時的安全防護措施，將安全判斷與工具執行解耦：它使用扁平化的文本工具規範來評估請求，同時保留原始的架構格式化規範以供執行。<lb/>在兩個具有代表性的基準測試和四個 LLMs 中，包括白盒和黑盒模型，SafeKeep 將有害請求的平均拒絕率從 23.8% 提高到 70.6%，並將觀察級提示注入下的平均攻擊成功率從 25.6% 降低到 2.5%。<lb/>它還超越了現有的安全防護措施，並保持了任務處理能力。<lb/>我們在 https://github.com/snowcatsmoking/SafeKeep 上發布了代碼和數據。
